doc.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Spirit, mortal mind and giving up smoking
summary: Williams speaks of the Great Spirit and Christian Science's immortal mind; talk drifts to smoking.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: And you always deal with the spirit of those that loved you. Like part Indian and part African. Okay. O Great Spirit, yes, the Great Spirit that you know is part of all of us. Some people say there’s more to mortal mind. I wonder about that sometimes.
Wanting mortal mind? I’ve never heard of this.
Wanting the Lord would be the immortal?
Yeah. There are some people who believe in that.
It takes a lot of explaining I guess.
Yeah. A woman who was a Christian Scientist and talked to me about that. That there’s only one immortal mind, which we tune in to or we don’t.

No I gave up smoking for three months and then I went back and then I go up and down. I cut them in half, but I’m more sensitive to them than I used to be. I didn’t use to. So I have to give it up now, because we’re really pushing our luck.
Well you remember when I smoked.
